synopsis: Wheel loaders are the booklet’s clearest nuisance-braking challenge because normal work can resemble a collision threat; its recommended starting domain is reverse-only, low-speed operation [f11395, f11397]. Vendor precedents are narrowly scoped: Volvo’s January 2023 system brakes in reverse at 3–15 km/h for 2–3 seconds on named models, while Cat’s May 2025 medium-loader system is reverse-only and can inhibit reverse engagement after at least 15 seconds stationary with an object in the critical zone [f1238, f1380, f356, f10637]. Front-end loaders were involved in 33% of 22 US surface-mine blind-area deaths from 2000 to mid-2006, but internationally comparable, exposure-adjusted rates were not found, so these counts cannot establish a reliable machine-type collision-rate ranking [f2985, f3238]. Virtual validation has some direct evidence—a 2025 radar hall experiment required manual material tuning and exposed missing double reflections, and a 2025 AGX digital twin was calibrated against a physical loader—but a 2024 digging simulation needed a friction coefficient of 2.0, flagged as a sim-to-field warning [f4421, f5049, f8292, f6090, f6376]. Major gaps remain in production-loader brake-delay distributions, peer-reviewed measured response times, production-scale vehicle-in-the-loop testing, and published vendor weather limits, false-intervention rates and validation methods [f252, f6065, f5342, f11394]. Safety planning must also account for abrupt-stop instability and operating exclusions: Komatsu advises disabling stop control on steep slopes, slippery or soft ground, with suspended loads and during trailer loading, while validated braking-related occupant-injury curves were not found [f10549, f10550, f3395].
